text: The walrus operator, a colon followed by equals, assigns a value and uses it in the same expression.
Here we compute the length, store it in n, and compare it to three, all in one line.
[chuckle] Then we reuse n inside the block, without ever computing the length twice.
That's the whole point — capture a value right where you test it, avoiding a separate line before the if.
[sniff] It's especially handy when a computation is expensive and you'd rather not repeat it.
We calculate the integer square root once, name it root, and use it both in the test and the message.
[sigh] The walrus also cleans up while loops that read until a sentinel value.
Each pass reads the next value, assigns it to v, and checks it against zero, all in the loop condition.
[groan] Use the walrus sparingly — in the right spot it's elegant, but overused it makes lines hard to read.
